summary: pgmigrations gains two additive nullable columns, state and refused_reason (cinatra#3031, epic #3023 W7). WHY: W7 splits the credential an extension migration runs under from the credential its ledger row is written with — the host keeps the lock and the ledger under its own role and switches to the extension's own role around the extension's statements only, so a statement that touches another table, another extension's table or the ledger is refused by the database itself. A refusal has to be RECORDED and must not read as already-run: without a state column the host can either write nothing (the next boot retries with no record that it ever failed) or write the row (the migration is skipped forever as though it had succeeded), and neither is a record. SHAPE: ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS state text and refused_reason text, no default, no backfill, no CHECK. NULL is every row written before the columns existed and every core row the library still writes itself, so NULL MEANS applied and the runner's read is spelled state IS DISTINCT FROM 'refused'. STRICTLY ADDITIVE: no row is rewritten, no existing read changes meaning, every consumer that selects name is untouched. This is the operator-upgrade twin of the idempotent ensure the extension runner performs at boot (ensureExtensionLedgerStateColumns in packages/migrations/src/extension-migrations.mjs), so a fresh database and an upgraded one land on one shape. DOWN drops both columns and with them every recorded refusal — the honest reverse of an additive change, degrading the read to what the ledger meant before. Unqualified name rides the runner's search_path (the app schema). SEQ 0098 — strictly greater than the max shipped seq on origin/main (core__0097 artifact-review-audit-first-party-renderer-kind). migrations/** is HIGH-RISK: owner approval required; the lane never merges.
